transcript: Yesterday, my boyfriend Paul and I attended Manahatta at The Public. Manahatta is Lenape for Manhattan, the island inhabited by the Lenape people prior to the European colonization. In this play, we simultaneously follow an ambitious woman working on Wall Street while reckoning with her Lenape ancestry and the Lenape people in the 1600s experiencing the mistreatment and genocide which expelled them from Manhattan. This play is about ownership, assimilation, history, the predatory nature of capitalism, and those who have used it to their advantage. I thought the concept and the structure of the play was wildly inventive, and although some of the writing felt stiff to me at times, the story was resonant and the performances were convincing. Overall a very thought provoking piece and a great meditation on the ways in which our histories and our todays converse with each other. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
